claims.text: SPS with pre-milled nanocrystalline powder is necessary to suppress grain growth and elemental segregation in the proposed Mg-transition-metal alloy.
The optimum SPS temperature is 925 ± 25 °C.
At 925 °C, SPS pressure-enhanced diffusion will overcome kinetic barriers to solid-solution formation.
Processing at 925 °C will avoid Mg volatility.
Processing at 925 °C will avoid brittle intermetallic-phase formation.
Mechanical alloying creates nanocrystallinity and high defect density that lower the activation barrier for solid-solution formation.
Rapid SPS heating and a short dwell provide sufficient mobility for densification while limiting Mg loss and segregation.
Quenching prevents secondary-phase precipitation that would occur during slow cooling.
Slow cooling of HfNbTaTiZr after sintering produces a multiphase structure.
Metastable single-phase formation proceeds by interface-controlled growth driven by mixing entropy and kinetic suppression of nucleation.
SPS at 925 °C for 10 minutes under 50 MPa, followed by rapid cooling, will trap a metastable single-phase structure.
The resulting relative density will exceed 98.5%.
The resulting material will have a single-phase-like BCC or HCP solid solution with negligible elemental segregation.
A homogeneous bulk microstructure will significantly improve oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to standard-sintered material.
The Vickers hardness will exceed 150 Hv because of solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement.
Standard pressure sintering at 800–1000 °C produces less than 90% relative density in the Mg-transition-metal system.
Standard pressure sintering in this window causes elemental segregation, brittle intermetallic phases, poor mechanical properties, and rapid oxidation.
Relative density falls below 95% when the sintering temperature is below 850 °C.
Mg volatility and excessive grain growth occur above 1000 °C or when dwell time exceeds 20 minutes.
Heating rates below 10 °C/min or omission of pre-milling cause segregation and Laves-phase-like precipitation.

contradictions.description: The optimum is initially specified as 925 ± 25 °C, whereas the uncertainty field expands the possible variation to ±50 °C.
The boundary places the onset of Mg volatility above 1000 °C, but the falsification rule expects a significant volatility increase at exactly 1000 °C relative to 925 °C.
